fixed.how: The switch-off session read (store.session) now accepts only sessions with no account (user_id IS NULL), which is what the switch-off sign-in writes. So a switch-on session that has not passed MFA, is idle, or belongs to a disabled user no longer becomes a '*' session on a switch-off site. With the decided pairing (beta off, live on) this also ties every session to the site that made it, with no sessions.site column.

Migration 20261119_022 adds identities.seed_verifier_sha256 (the sha256 of the verifier the seed last wrote, never the verifier itself) and fills it for the seed's own identity. AccountStore.seed copies EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER only while sha256(verifier) still equals that mark. After a password change or reset on the switch-on site the identity belongs to the account and is never overwritten (logged account_seed_password_kept). The switch-off sign-in still reads the environment value directly. The recorded rule changed, so the README switch table and the seed docstring were updated.

fixed.how: Migrations 20261119_020 and _021 add site (NOT NULL DEFAULT 'beta', CHECK beta|live) to edge_bff.jobs and edge_bff.backtest_jobs. Store.submit, Store.claim and _promote carry and filter the site. BacktestStore(store, site) claims, reaps and prunes only its own site's jobs. The AI worker's claim is bound to the app's site (worker.claim, the same pattern as worker.access). Per-loop switches replace the single all-or-nothing switch: EDGE_AI_WORKER_ENABLED (unset means beta only; true on live is refused), EDGE_BACKTEST_LOOP_ENABLED, EDGE_HOUSEKEEPING_ENABLED, and EDGE_EMAIL_ENABLED (the sender runs only with the switch on, so only on live). EDGE_WORKER_ENABLED=false still turns every loop off.

Duplicate of R2-7 plus R2-2, closed by the same fixes. config.validate also refuses the mixed pairings: EDGE_SITE=live without EDGE_MULTIUSER, and the beta with EDGE_MULTIUSER on outside EDGE_ENVIRONMENT=local.

Duplicate of R2-7. The email outbox needs no site column: only the switch-on site (live) writes it and runs the sender. The hourly housekeeping runs in its own task, and an advisory try-lock on each purge stops two sites running the same purge at once.

Parts 1 and 2 are fixed as R2-7 and R2-2. EDGE_SITE (beta|live, default beta) is in place, and the live site masks every principal: principal.beta_only, live_view and Auth.site_view. On live nothing in the Monitor or admin tabs, no admin right from rights.py and no lab item is ever held, '*' included ('*' reads as every catalog flag that is not beta-only). allow_of never sends '*' from live. Auth.need answers 404 NOT_FOUND for those capabilities before the session is read, and /monitor and /c/<id> answer 404 too. MFA is still decided by the account's own grants, so user #1 needs MFA on live. Part 3 (the expand-then-contract order for 20261118_001 and 3c step 4) needs no code and is written into the notes for the records track. The pending test moved into apps/edge-bff/tests/ and was changed to the decided pairing (see notes).

What can be checked from one process: config.shared_key_marks() writes a 12-hex HMAC mark of EDGE_SESSION_SECRET, EDGE_CODE_SECRET and EDGE_MFA_KEY into every startup_done log line. The two services' lines then show whether they hold the same values, without logging any secret. The rule itself (edge-bff-live takes all three as ${{edge-bff.NAME}} references) is in the railway.ts comment block and in the notes for CONTRACT 16.

The secrets part is handled as in R2-8. The log-mode guard no longer accepts EDGE_ENVIRONMENT=dev, which is also the live site's Railway environment. Log mode with the switch on now needs EDGE_ENVIRONMENT=local or an explicit EDGE_EMAIL_LOG_ALLOWED=true. That flag exists for a deliberate test on the live site before the Resend key, with no real person (the user asked on 2026-11-19 to test directly on weblive). While it is on, email_log_mode_allowed is logged at every start.

The start-up now runs as one attempt under a lock: readiness, seed, catalog names, seed plan, then the loops. The attempt runs in the lifespan, is retried every EDGE_POLL_SECONDS and on each /ready, and /ready answers 503 until it succeeds. No loop starts before that, the backtest loop included (store.ready reads no backtest table, so the reason for the old comment still holds). With the switch on, a failing seed fails the attempt. New log lines: startup_not_ready and startup_done.

The same start-up fix as R2-3. EDGE_WORKER_ENABLED, EDGE_EMAIL_ENABLED and the new loop switches are parsed with switch_of, so a typo stops the start. email_sender_off is logged at error level whenever the switch is on and no sender runs.

The purges left the AI loop for worker.Housekeeping, a task of their own that also runs on live, where there is no AI loop. Each purge in store.PURGES (sessions, throttle, pending) now has its own transaction and its own try. It deletes at most 500 rows per batch (by key) and at most 20 batches per turn. A failed purge is retried after a backoff that doubles up to an hour, is logged as housekeeping_failed by error class, and is skipped while another instance holds its try-lock. purge_pending and throttle.purge take an optional limit and return the row count. BacktestLoop.run now runs prune (by site, batched), reap and claim each in its own try, and a failed prune backs off.

fixed.how: Migration 20261119_023 adds plain btree indexes on sessions(user_id), email_codes(user_id), admin_audit(actor_user_id), admin_audit(target_user_id), subscriptions(user_id, starts_at DESC) and user_capability_overrides(created_by_user_id). Its $verify$ block refuses any foreign key to users that lacks a leading non-partial index. Bounded EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) at the finder's sizes: purging 200 pending accounts went from 5830.7 ms to 27.4 ms; the resolve for an ended plan from 4.68 ms to 0.66 ms; the session cap from 8.96 ms to 0.13 ms; revoke_all from 9.27 ms to 0.24 ms. The site claims use the existing partial indexes (0.05 ms and 0.15 ms), so no index was added for site.

not_fixed.reason: No code change is needed; the refuters agree. The ordering rule is written into the notes for the records track (EXEC 'Production environment'): never pair a live edge-bff older than the 3b follow-up with 20261118_001, and hold 3c step 4 until every edge-bff sends the owner headers.

decisions_needed.context: The live website (edge-bff-live, app.edgefinance.id) is for users; the beta (edge-bff) is for the admin only, as the user decided ('beta hanya admin'). The decision does not say whether the admin's own account (user #1, edge-private, which holds every capability) may also sign in on the live site. As built, it can: it needs the authenticator code there too, and it sees the live site masked, with no Monitor, no admin pages, no point-in-time Flow and no lab items, much as a paying user would.
decisions_needed.options: A) Keep this: the admin can check the live site as a user sees it, with MFA. B) Refuse user #1's sign-in on the live site, so the admin works only on the beta.
decisions_needed.recommendation: A: it lets the admin check the live site after each push to live, and the mask plus MFA keeps the beta-only tools off the public site.

fixed.how: edge-bff now uses one rule, terminal_access.relayed (apps/edge-bff/app/terminal_access.py:303), for every terminal-api answer it relays: forward_terminal, relay_cut and PageFiles all go through it. A terminal-api 401, any 403 other than capability_required, a 400 about edge-bff's own owner headers, and every 5xx become 503 TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE in the contract shape, logged as terminal_refused with the upstream status and code. A 429 becomes 429 LIMIT_REACHED with details.limit terminal.<quota>, allowed, retry_after_s and the Retry-After header. A 400 about the request is answered 400 INVALID_INPUT, and a 404 is answered 404 NOT_FOUND; both carry terminal-api's code as details.reason. capability_required becomes CAPABILITY_REQUIRED with its display name. terminal-api's message text never reaches the page. On terminal-api, take() now raises quota_exceeded with quota, limit, window and retry_after_s, and sets the Retry-After header (wait_error). The wait comes from Store.frees_in: the seconds until the rolling window lets the refused request fit, read only on a refusal and never longer than the window. The service ceiling and the sign-in throttle send Retry-After too. In the Terminal page, live.ts now shows the contract's words instead of the code. M260 (public_data) was not applied; it needs the user's go.
fixed.tests: tests/test_cp0_terminal_relay.py: 2 now pass. New edge-bff tests/test_terminal_fix_round.py: a 16-case mapping table plus a route-level test (session kept, Retry-After, byte relay). New terminal-api tests/test_terminal_fix_round.py: the 429 fields, and frees_in on PostgreSQL 16. Changed because they locked the pass-through that CONTRACT section 3 forbids: test_terminal.py:84 and test_gateway_leaves_the_reference_names_to_terminal_api (now the contract shape with details.reason), and test_terminal_access.py test_a_cut_terminal_api_refuses_passes_through, renamed to ..._reaches_the_page_in_the_contract_shape.

fixed.how: PageFiles now answers a grant's 429 through the same rule: 429 LIMIT_REACHED with details and Retry-After, replacing <FAMILY>_QUOTA, and the QUOTA message is removed (apps/edge-bff/app/pages.py page_file). terminal-api sends the header and the structured fields (see R1-1).
fixed.tests: tests/test_c_p3a_probes.py -k retry_after: 2 now pass. Changed as the refuters said: test_radar.py:123-125 now expects LIMIT_REACHED with details and Retry-After, and its FakeHttp sends terminal-api's new fields.

fixed.how: Read side: terminal_access.capabilities now maps every value onto the wire. history_days above 36600 is sent as 36600. A value of 0 is sent as 0, which terminal-api now accepts as the empty window (entitlements MIN_HISTORY_DAYS); check() then refuses files, bundle, cut and history first with 403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED terminal.history_days, so the page files keep working (the code refuter's correction). A ticker outside ^[A-Z0-9]{1,12}$ is dropped and logged (count only). A quota of 0 is now 403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED naming the limit instead of a 429, which was the refuters' 'other site'. Catalog side: new migration database/migrations/20261119_050_edge_bff_capability_domains.sql, not applied, added to tests/conftest.py, with a $verify$ block. It adds value_min, value_max and item_pattern to edge_bff.capabilities, and capability_value_check is replaced so it reads them after the shape check, with a hint that names the domain and gives an example. A new trigger, capabilities_domain_holds, refuses a domain change that a stored value would no longer fit. Domains set: terminal.history_days 1-36600; terminal.tickers 0-500 items matching ^[A-Z0-9]{1,12}$, which also closes the case where a list of about 900 tickers gave 503 on every call; the four Terminal quotas 1-10^9. fixed.how: Option (a), using the task's reading of D3 = B ('no list of other tickers'). terminal-api now answers an owner whose plan lacks the dataset 'reference' with its own copy of each reference file (new apps/terminal-api/app/refcut.py). Which rows are kept is read from each file's own columns: a 'ticker' column keeps the plan's tickers; the broker list keeps its rows only when the plan holds 'broker'; any other file, today the stock lists, has no rows (fail closed). The copy is announced in the shape of a cut, '/api/terminal/v1/reference/<name>/cut?sha256=…'. It is served by GET /reference/{name}/cut and counted when served, with one audit row 'refcut/<name>/<sha>'. It is built from the published file after checking its sha256, uses deterministic gzip, and is cached. A file that cannot be filtered answers 503 reference_unavailable and is never served whole. A plan holding 'reference' gets the published file as before. ROUTE_ACCESS marks both reference routes 'filtered'. edge-bff now forwards reference/* without refusing it and relays the copy byte for byte (main.py TERMINAL_BYTES). The page draws as it does today. live.ts now tells a plan whose list holds no published ticker so (NO_TICKER) instead of crashing on tickers[0].

result.notes:
My notes for the records track are in verification/edge_multiuser/fix_round/terminal.md (committed). That file has, for each finding, the root cause with file:line evidence, the fix, the tests and the tests changed with reasons. It also lists exactly what CONTRACT.md (sections 3 and 8b, including the tests-per-stage line, the 3e 'search marks locked tickers' wording, the rollback floor and the dataset order rule), ERRORS_AND_SOLUTIONS.md, DATABASE_SCHEMA.md, DATABASE_CHANGELOG.md and EXEC.md must say; RAILWAY_CHANGELOG.md needs nothing. I did not edit any shared record.

Tests changed, and why:
- test_terminal.py:84 and test_radar.py:123-125 locked the old flat shape and the refuters named them.
- test_terminal_access.py (FREE_REFUSED for references, the cut 404 shape, quota 0) and terminal-api test_phase3c.py (SECOND_PATHS for /reference, two BAD rows) are 3c's own tests, and the design they test changed.
- In test_phase2_fix_round.py, history_days '0' became '1', as the refuter asked.
- In test_c2_e2e_people.py, the answer-set lines changed as the test itself foresaw; its assertion is unchanged.
- The fakes that stand in for terminal-api now echo the applied header, as the new terminal-api does.

Other changes:
- SCREENER_ONBOARDING.md line pointers were moved with the lines of both main.py files, which the screener-worker pointer test checks.
- The edge-bff and terminal-api READMEs were updated to match the changes.

Deploy order: terminal-api must be deployed before or together with this edge-bff. That only matters once the switch is on, because with it off every principal holds '*'.

I did not push, deploy, call Railway or touch any remote database. My local cluster fx_terminal (port 55561) has been stopped.
